instructions: sys1rust is a local runtime for Laya System 1 decision models (ModernBERT or mmBERT encoder, a 2-layer transformer decision head, a scorer at per-option [MASK] markers). runtime/ is a Rust workspace: laya-core (tokenizer, request parsing, sequence layout, decoding; no GPU code), laya-mlx (the forward pass on Apple's MLX through mlx-rs; custom Metal kernels, compiled at run time through the vendored mlx-sys C API, are being added in follow-up PRs), sys1d (an axum HTTP server that must match upstream `laya serve` byte for byte at the protocol level) and sys1-bench (bench adapter and probe). bench/ is a Python harness that runs contenders on shared workloads and compares answers to upstream fp32 references. results/ and research/ are measured write-ups. Review for correctness first: answers must stay identical to upstream Laya (choice agreement of 99% or more against bench/reference, probabilities within about 1e-3 of the old path for pure speed changes). Then for performance on the inference path, then for clarity. Point out claims in docs that the code or data in the PR does not support.

rules.rule: A change to the forward pass, masks, dtypes, reduction order, tokenization or decoding must say how it was checked against the upstream reference answers. Flag any change that can alter a chosen answer without such a check.

MLX arrays are lazy. Flag host synchronizations on the inference path (eval, item, as_slice, to_vec, printing arrays) that are not needed, and integer `index(i)` calls in mlx-rs, which gather a copy instead of taking a view.

A custom Metal kernel that replaces MLX ops must compute what those ops compute: the same formula (for RoPE, MLX's angle arithmetic), the same accumulation and rounding precision, and the same output shape and memory layout the next op expects. It needs a test that compares it to the MLX path it replaces at more than one shape, including packed (unpadded) batches. Flag index math that can read or write out of bounds: grids larger than the work, the last partial row, packed index arrays, and vector loads that assume alignment or a dimension divisible by the vector width.

Calls into mlx-sys (the mlx-c C API) are unsafe. Flag handles (arrays, vectors, kernel objects, kernel configs, streams) that leak or are freed twice, non-zero return codes that are ignored, unsafe impl Send or Sync without a comment saying why it holds, and inputs dropped while MLX can still read them.

A custom kernel must not make the runtime fail on an MLX build, macOS version or chip where it does not compile or run. The MLX path it replaces stays available behind a setting, and a kernel that cannot be built is detected at model load with a clear message or a fallback, never in the middle of a request.

The model runs in fp16. Flag values that overflow fp16 (for example mask constants below -65504), silent promotion of activations to fp32 on the hot path, and comparisons that assume exact equality between differently shaped matmuls.

Any cache keyed by request shape (masks, gather indices, compiled traces, custom kernel instantiations, buffers) must have a bound or a documented reason why the key space is small. A long-running server sees many distinct lengths.

sys1d must match upstream laya serve: status codes, error `detail` strings, header names (Server-Timing, X-Inference-Time-Ms, Retry-After), response key order and request limits. Flag any divergence that is not documented as intentional.
In sys1d, a panic or error in one request must not poison shared state or take down the inference thread; admission must stay bounded; client-controlled text must be sanitized before logging.

Crates under runtime/crates must not call Python or depend on a Python environment at run time. Build-time use of a prebuilt MLX from a Python wheel is a known packaging gap, not a runtime dependency.
Scripts and docs must not hard-code a user's home directory or other machine-specific absolute paths. Resolve paths relative to the script or repo root.
